postTitle: Cash Flow Forecasting: Will You Have Enough?
topic: Cash runway: how long your money lasts if your pay stops

assumptions.notes: Easy access savings €18,300 (money that can be moved within 48 hours without penalty). Investments and pension €45,000, which do not count toward runway. Real monthly costs €4,575 (the year average including once a year costs, from day 1). Runway = €18,300 ÷ €4,575 = 4.0 months. With the budget figure of €4,000: €18,300 ÷ €4,000 = 4.6 months. If monthly costs rise to €6,100: €18,300 ÷ €6,100 = 3.0 months. Illustrative.

hookVariants.narration: If your pay stopped today, how many months would your money last? Most people guess. It is one division.
Eighteen thousand in savings sounds like a year of safety. For most people it is about four months.
Your runway is probably shorter than you think, and the reason is a number you already know.

beats.narration: Jiri has eighteen thousand three hundred euros in easy access savings.
He also has forty five thousand in investments and his pension. For runway, none of that counts.
His real costs, once a year bills included, are four thousand five hundred and seventy five a month.
beats.subtext: Real costs, once a year bills included

beats.narration: Eighteen thousand three hundred, divided by that, is four months.
With his budget figure of four thousand, he would think it was four point six. The once a year costs take that away.
beats.subtext: Use real costs, not the budget

beats.narration: And runway moves. If his costs rise to six thousand one hundred a month, the same savings last three months.
So the check is one line. Easy access cash, divided by real monthly costs. Redo it whenever your costs change.
beats.subtext: Easy access cash ÷ real monthly costs

caption.instagram:
If your pay stopped today, how many months would your money last? Most people guess. It is one division.

Jiri has €18,300 in easy access savings. His €45,000 in investments and his pension do not count: runway is only money you can reach within a couple of days without a penalty. His real costs, once a year bills included, are €4,575 a month. So his runway is four months.

Using his budget figure of €4,000 he would think 4.6. And if his costs rise to €6,100, the same savings last three months.

The runway check: easy access cash ÷ real monthly costs. Redo it whenever your costs change.
